title: The "friends of" organizations behind departments
question: Which departments still have a support organization that raises and holds money for them, what has it given, what does the City pay it, and who funds it?
finding: The Controller's June 2026 audit lists 12 support organizations as of November 2025 (9 active, 2 developing, 1 defunct), against the 19 "Friends of" organizations departments reported in 2020; the defunct one is the San Francisco Parks Alliance, which held the Public Works accounts the Controller reviewed in 2020. Its returns show net assets falling from $17.2 million at June 2020 to minus $566,155 at June 2024, while the City paid it $22.8 million from fiscal 2017. The largest giver named for the department it supports is on neither Controller list: San Francisco Police Community Foundation gave Police gifts valued at $13.4 million in the two years of gift reports. Foundations in the grants file paid the organizations in the table $143.2 million. For 1 of them a funder, or a payor who gave at an official's request, is also paid by the same department: for the Parks Alliance, Pacific Gas and Electric Company ($16.3 million); Recology San Francisco ($9.1 million); Golden State Warriors ($124,040).
how: The list is the Controller's: Exhibit 1 of the June 2026 audit (organizations active or developing in November 2025, by department) and the table of "Friends of" organizations in the September 2020 review; each name is checked against the document text. To that are added donors in the gift reports whose name carries the name of the department they give to and the word foundation, friends, alliance, conservancy or society. For each: gifts it gave City departments in the gift reports (November 2024 to October 2026), City payments to it (fiscal 2017 to 2027, all departments, and its own department), the latest tax return on file here (returns are held only for organizations the City pays $750,000 or more), grants paid to it by Bay Area private foundations and large community foundations (returns for tax years 2020 to 2025), and payments made to it at a City official's request. A funder is shown in the last column when the organization's own department paid a payee of the same name $25,000 or more.
limits: A support organization exists to give to its department, and since September 2020 each must have a written agreement approved by the City Attorney and the Controller; nothing here says any of them broke it. Tax returns do not name donors, so 'who funds it' is limited to foundations that file their own returns and to payments reported as made at an official's request: company and individual donors, the route in the Public Works case, cannot be seen in any file here. A funder that is also paid by the department is often a utility, a refuse collector or a health plan that every department pays as a customer, which is an ordinary overlap. City payments to an organization are usually grants for services and are not gifts returning. Community Initiatives and Collective Impact are fiscal sponsors or grantees with many other programmes, so their figures cover far more than the fund the Controller lists. An organization on neither list may have no duty to be on one. Organizations are matched by name across files.
